about: Funding sources for the Gap Closer prototype. Names, URLs and the 'facts' lines come from lanes/3-fund-it/data/DATA-SOURCES.md (checked 2026-11-06 by the organizers). Every number inside 'placeholder' is INVENTED for the prototype and must be replaced with current program terms before anyone relies on it.
placeholder_note: PLACEHOLDER values: award_per_home, max_total, probability, prep_months (time to prepare and submit) and months_to_funds (submission to money) are made up so the advisor has something to rank. They are not program terms. Lowered on 2026-11-07 to conservative per-home figures (roughly a third of the first guesses) so no single source looks like it closes the gap alone.

sources.name: HOME Investment Partnerships
sources.agency: HUD, through California HCD or a local participating jurisdiction
sources.pays_for: Affordable homeownership and housing activities. Buyer income caps follow the State HOME income limits.
facts: State HOME income limits are a separate PDF, effective June 1, 2026.
sources.next_step: Ask the city or county housing office whether it receives HOME directly or applies through HCD, and when the next round opens.

sources.name: Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
sources.agency: HUD, to entitlement cities and counties, or through HCD for smaller cities
sources.pays_for: Community development activities chosen locally, which can include housing.
sources.next_step: Check whether this city is a CDBG entitlement jurisdiction and read its current Action Plan.

sources.name: Self-Help Homeownership Opportunity Program (SHOP)
sources.pays_for: Land and infrastructure for sweat-equity and volunteer-based builders, not whole-home costs.
facts: Funds land and infrastructure for sweat-equity builders, which limits what a dollar can pay for.
sources.next_step: Only pursue if the project uses a sweat-equity model. Confirm eligibility on HUD Exchange.

sources.name: CalHome (Homeownership Super NOFA)
sources.pays_for: State homeownership loans to local agencies and nonprofits: down payment, rehab, self-help.
facts: HCD bundles homeownership programs in its Homeownership Super NOFA (HOSN).
sources.next_step: Read the current HOSN notice for round dates and per-unit limits.

sources.name: CalHFA MyHome Assistance
sources.pays_for: A junior loan to the buyer for down payment or closing costs.
facts: The CalHFA page says up to 3.5% (FHA) or 3% (conventional).

formula.source: CalHFA homebuyer programs page: up to 3% (conventional) or 3.5% (FHA). Via lanes/3-fund-it/data/DATA-SOURCES.md, checked 2026-11-06.
formula.basis_note: ASSUMPTION: uses the lower 3% (conventional) and applies it to the price; the page summary does not say what the percentage is of. Confirm with a CalHFA lender.

placeholder.why_counts: ASSUMPTION: buyer help raises what the family can pay at closing, which narrows the gap.

sources.next_step: Have the buyer talk with a CalHFA-approved lender. This is the buyer's loan, not the project's.

sources.name: CalHFA Dream For All
sources.pays_for: A shared appreciation loan to the buyer.
facts: The page says up to 20%, not to exceed $150,000, with voucher registration and a randomized drawing.
Search results (not read at the source) say funds ran out in 2023. Availability is not confirmed.

formula.source: calhfa.ca.gov/dream: up to 20%, not to exceed $150,000. Via lanes/3-fund-it/data/DATA-SOURCES.md, checked 2026-11-06. Funds not confirmed.
formula.basis_note: ASSUMPTION: applies the 20% to the price; the page summary does not say what the percentage is of.

placeholder.why_counts: ASSUMPTION: buyer help raises what the family can pay at closing, which narrows the gap.

sources.next_step: Check whether a new round is open before counting on it. Entry is by drawing.

sources.name: CalHFA Forgivable Equity Builder
sources.pays_for: A forgivable 0% buyer loan (per news reports).
facts: No official page was found. A 2022 CalHFA board handout described it as winding down.
sources.next_step: Do not model it as open.

sources.name: Orange County Housing Finance Trust
sources.pays_for: Countywide housing funding through a NOFA. No homeownership text was found on its home page.
facts: The programs page loads and shows a NOFA.
sources.next_step: Read the current NOFA and confirm ownership projects are eligible.

sources.name: Santa Ana My First Home
sources.pays_for: City down-payment loan to the buyer.
facts: The page loads with the title My First Home Program. Loan terms came from a search snippet, not the page: read it.

placeholder.why_counts: ASSUMPTION: buyer help raises what the family can pay at closing, which narrows the gap.

sources.next_step: Read the program page for current loan terms and income limits.

sources.name: Garden Grove First-Time Homebuyer Program
sources.pays_for: City down-payment help, under its 2025 guidelines.
facts: The 2025 guidelines PDF loads (22 MB). Dollar tiers came from a search snippet only.

placeholder.why_counts: ASSUMPTION: buyer help raises what the family can pay at closing, which narrows the gap.

sources.next_step: Read the guidelines PDF for tiers and income limits.

sources.name: Anaheim down-payment program
facts: No program could be confirmed. The city site blocks automated fetches, and one URL seen elsewhere is an unrelated plan page.

sources.name: Costa Mesa down-payment program
facts: No program could be confirmed. The city site blocks automated fetches.

sources.name: Fullerton down-payment program
facts: No program could be confirmed. The city site blocks automated fetches.

sources.name: State housing bond
sources.pays_for: Unknown. No homeownership set-aside was confirmed.
facts: The HCD URLs tried returned 404. Prop 1 (2024) is the behavioral health bond, not a homeownership bond.
sources.next_step: Confirm with HCD whether any current bond has homeownership money.

sources.name: Local housing bond or tax-exempt financing
sources.pays_for: PLACEHOLDER category so the prototype can show where a local bond would sit.
facts: No local bond program has been researched for this prototype.
sources.next_step: Ask the city and county whether a local housing bond or measure funds ownership homes.

sources.name: FHLBank San Francisco WISH
sources.agency: Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco, through member banks
sources.pays_for: Grants for first-time buyer down-payment help, delivered through member banks.

placeholder.why_counts: ASSUMPTION: buyer help raises what the family can pay at closing, which narrows the gap.

sources.next_step: Find a participating member bank and ask when its WISH allocation opens.

sources.name: FHLBank San Francisco Affordable Housing Program (AHP)
sources.agency: Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco, with a member bank sponsor
sources.pays_for: Competitive grants and subsidized advances for affordable housing.
sources.next_step: Line up a member bank sponsor and read the current AHP round dates.

sources.name: Bank Community Reinvestment Act commitments
sources.agency: Banks regulated under the CRA (OCC overview)
sources.pays_for: A lever: banks' CRA obligations can motivate grants, sponsorships or below-market loans.
facts: The FFIEC CRA data page returned 403 and is unverified.
sources.next_step: Ask local branch community development officers about CRA-motivated grants.

sources.name: Low Income Investment Fund
sources.pays_for: Loans for affordable housing. A loan bridges timing but does not close the gap by itself.

placeholder.why_counts: A loan must be repaid, so it is shown for cash flow but not counted toward the gap.

sources.next_step: Use for bridge or construction financing while grants arrive.
